task_completion.description: The chest CT scan for patient LIDC-IDRI-0001 is loaded into the 3D Slicer workspace.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 3D Slicer interface shows axial, sagittal, and coronal views of a chest CT scan; the Data module or Subject Hierarchy lists a volume named 'LIDC-IDRI-0001' or similar.

task_completion.description: A new segmentation node is created and named 'Airways'.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Segment Editor module or the Subject Hierarchy shows a segmentation node or segment explicitly named 'Airways'.

task_completion.description: The agent uses segmentation tools (e.g., Threshold, Grow from Seeds, or Paint) to isolate the trachea and bronchi.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the Segment Editor active with tools like 'Threshold' or 'Grow from Seeds' being configured, and colored overlays appearing specifically within the dark airway lumens in the slice views.

task_completion.description: The segmentation is confined to the internal airways and does not include the air outside the patient's body.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The colored segmentation mask is visible only inside the patient's chest/neck area; no colored mask is visible in the black space surrounding the patient's skin.

task_completion.description: The segmentation correctly captures the tracheobronchial tree structure.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 3D view or slice views show a continuous tubular structure representing the trachea branching into the left and right mainstem bronchi.

task_completion.description: The segmentation is exported/saved to the specific file path ~/Documents/SlicerData/Exports/airways_segmentation.seg.nrrd.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Export to files' dialog or a terminal 'ls' command shows the file 'airways_segmentation.seg.nrrd' in the specified directory.

integrity.description: The agent used the 3D Slicer GUI tools rather than just executing a pre-written script or terminal command to generate the file.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the Segment Editor effects, sliders, or the 'Add' segment button.

integrity.description: The segmentation mask was actually generated from the loaded volume, not by loading a pre-existing mask file.
integrity.visual_evidence: The VLM should see the progression of the segmentation mask growing or being painted over several frames, rather than it appearing instantly in its final form.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply rename an existing file to match the target filename.
integrity.visual_evidence: The 'Save' or 'Export' dialog in Slicer is visible with the correct path and filename being typed or selected.

privileged_info_for_vlm: For patient LIDC-IDRI-0001, a valid airway segmentation should have a volume between 50 mL and 300 mL. The mean Hounsfield Unit (HU) value of the segmented area must be -800 HU or lower (representing air). The segmentation should ideally consist of a single connected component representing the trachea and major bronchi.
